thread:
Alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's v2->v3 rollout we saw a small but consistent uptick in 4xx/500s from legacy clients. Not catastrophic but we should discuss telemetry and a fast mitigation path.
Maria: Saw that in dashboards too. Error spike aligns with clients that still send `X-Client-Version: 2.*`.
Jia: Quick question: are these real errors, or just new stricter validation rejecting older request shape?
Alex: Mostly validation. Payload shape changes cause our new router to drop requests earlier. A few genuine 500s tied to unexpected nulls in parsing.
Kyle: Suggestion: enable a short-lived compatibility shim that accepts the legacy request shape and rewrites to v3 internal representation. Keep it behind a flag and heavy telemetry.
Maria: Agreed. We need two things: (1) events so we can count affected clients + request patterns, and (2) a safe shim with rate limits + opt-out header.
Sam: I can add metrics. I'll instrument: `compat.legacy_request.count`, `compat.rewrite.success`, `compat.rewrite.fail_reason`. Also tag by `client_version` and `route`.
InfraBot: Deploy job queued: canary to infra-canary-2, rollout window 30m. See: https://ci.redwood/workflows/4523
Jia: For the shim behavior, can we make it idempotent and side-effect free for replays? We must avoid reprocessing when rewrite changes shape of idempotent id fields.
Kyle: Good call. Implementation notes: 1) map legacy param `prompt_text` -> `input` 2) normalize `stop_sequences` shape 3) attach header `X-Compat-Handled: v2-to-v3` on successful rewrite
Maria: Also return a deprecation header to the client so we can surface in logs: `X-Deprecation-Notice: v2 removed, migrate to v3 by 2025-06-01`. Start conservative.
Alex: Telemetry + headers sound right. Operational constraints: shim must auto-disable if rewrite failure rate > 1% for a route, and we should expose a toggle per-route in console.
Sam: I'll add alerting: `compat.rewrite.fail_rate > 0.01` (5m) -> Pager to eng-platform-oncall. Also dashboard widget and per-route histograms.
Maria: Security check: make sure the shim doesn't bypass auth checks. It should operate after auth but before validation.
Kyle: Implementation plan: PR that adds a `CompatMiddleware` in router stack (after auth). Config flags: `compat.enabled`, `compat.per_route_exceptions`, `compat.max_qps`.
Alex: Can we also emit a short sample of rewritten payload to S3 for triage (scrubbed)? Ticket for retention policy needed.
Jia: Only store hashed client_id + truncated request body. No PII. Put in `s3://redwood-compat-samples/` with 7-day TTL.
Sam: Will include sample_count metric to track how many samples we capture.
Maria: Timeline: canary tomorrow 09:30, monitor for 24h, then 50% rollout if OK, full rollout in 72h. If alerts fire, rollback immediately.
Alex: Ops action items: @Sam add metrics + alert, @Kyle sketch middleware PR, @Jia add data retention ticket, @Maria add console toggle + docs, I'll own rollout and communications.
Sam: On it. I'll create PR and dashboard link: https://dash.redwood/compat-1719
Kyle: Drafting middleware PR now. Quick snippet for review: ```python
class CompatMiddleware:
    def __call__(self, req, next):
        if req.headers.get("X-Client-Version", "").startswith("2."):
            try:
                req = rewrite_v2_to_v3(req)
                req.headers["X-Compat-Handled"] = "v2-to-v3"
                metrics.increment("compat.rewrite.success", tags={"route": req.route})
            except Exception as e:
                metrics.increment("compat.rewrite.fail", tags={"route": req.route, "reason": str(e)})
                raise
        return next(req)
```
Jia: That looks good. Add a defensive timeout in rewrite and circuit-breaker to prevent latency amplification.
Kyle: Will add. Also will include `compat.max_latency_ms` config.
Maria: I'll draft a short blurb for the API changelog and customer-facing support note explaining the deprecation schedule.
Alex: Perfect. Let's reconvene after canary metrics. Thanks. :thumbsup:
